title: Australia Skilled Migration Visa 2026: 189, 190 & 491
metaDescription: Australia skilled migration visa 2026: 65-point minimum, subclass 189, 190 and 491 compared, fees from AUD 6,135, English points and how SkillSelect works.
headline: Australia Skilled Migration Visa 2026: Full Guide

sections.title: The Three Points-Tested Visas
sections.content:
Australia skilled migration runs through three points-tested visas. Subclass 189, Skilled Independent, needs no sponsor or nominator and grants permanent residence from day one. Subclass 190, Skilled Nominated, needs nomination by a state or territory government and adds five points. Subclass 491, Skilled Work Regional, needs regional nomination or family sponsorship, adds fifteen points, and leads to the permanent Subclass 191 visa after three years in a regional area.

All three require the same foundations: an occupation on the relevant skilled occupation list, a positive skills assessment from the authorised assessing body, an Expression of Interest submitted through SkillSelect, and an invitation to apply. You must be under 45 when invited, and you must meet at least Competent English.

sections.title: The Points Test Explained
sections.content:
The points test scores you out of 100 before additional factors, with a pass mark of 65 points, but 65 is only the floor. Most invitations for Subclass 189 and 190 in 2026 go to candidates with 85 points or more, especially in competitive fields such as engineering and ICT. Age is worth up to 30 points, with the maximum band at 25 to 32 years, falling to 15 points at 40 to 44.

English is the easiest lever for many applicants. Competent English earns no points, Proficient English earns 10 points, and Superior English earns 20 points, which means IELTS 8.0 or PTE 79 or above in each skill. Skilled employment adds up to 20 points, a bachelor or master degree adds 15 points, a doctorate adds 20, and state nomination adds 5 points for Subclass 190 or 15 for Subclass 491.

sections.title: Fees, Places and Processing in 2026
sections.content:
The 2026-27 permanent Migration Program is set at 185,000 places, with about 71 percent, or 132,240 places, in the Skilled stream. The base application charge for a main applicant is 6,135 Australian dollars for Subclass 189 and 6,140 dollars for Subclass 190 and 491. Processing for skilled and permanent residence categories currently takes roughly six and a half to ten months.

Planning levels are targets, not guarantees, and invitation rounds vary by occupation and points. An Expression of Interest stays valid for two years, and you should update it whenever your points improve, for example after a better English score or an extra year of skilled work. Fees and thresholds change regularly, so confirm them on the Department of Home Affairs website before you apply.

sections.title: How to Apply Step by Step
sections.content:
Start by checking that your occupation is on the skilled occupation list for your chosen subclass, then obtain a positive skills assessment from the relevant authority, such as Engineers Australia for engineers or the Australian Nursing and Midwifery Accreditation Council for nurses. Take an approved English test and gather your documents, including qualifications, employment references and identity papers.

Next, submit your Expression of Interest through SkillSelect and wait for an invitation. If invited, you generally have 60 days to lodge your visa application, pay the fee, and complete health and character checks. Keep your points accurate throughout, because a wrong claim can lead to refusal even after an invitation.

faqs.q: How many points do I need for Australian skilled migration?
faqs.a: You need at least 65 points to submit an Expression of Interest for Subclass 189, 190 or 491, but 65 is only the eligibility floor. In 2026 most invitations for Subclass 189 and 190 go to candidates with 85 points or more, especially in engineering and ICT. Aim for Superior English, extra skilled employment and, where possible, state nomination.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Subclass 189, 190 and 491?
faqs.a: Subclass 189 is the independent permanent visa with no sponsor, while Subclass 190 needs nomination by a state or territory and adds five points. Subclass 491 is a provisional regional visa that needs regional nomination or family sponsorship, adds fifteen points, and leads to the permanent Subclass 191 visa after three years living and working in a regional area.

faqs.q: What English score do I need for Australian skilled migration?
faqs.a: You need at least Competent English, which is IELTS 6.0 or PTE 50 in each skill, to qualify. Proficient English, IELTS 7.0 or PTE 65, earns 10 points, while Superior English, IELTS 8.0 or PTE 79, earns 20 points and often decides whether you receive an invitation. English tests are valid for a limited period, so time your test carefully.

faqs.q: How much does an Australian skilled visa cost in 2026?
faqs.a: The base application charge for a main applicant is 6,135 Australian dollars for Subclass 189 and 6,140 dollars for Subclass 190 and 491, as checked in late 2026. Partners and children pay additional charges, and skills assessments, English tests, health checks and police clearances cost extra. Fees change regularly, so confirm the current amount on the Home Affairs website.
